patients.summary: High school science teacher who joined in 2023 with hypercholesterolemia and chronic low back pain; hypertension diagnosed late 2024. A 2025 flame burn of the abdominal wall led to excision and grafting complicated by postoperative ileus, and in March 2026 he survived a refractory VF arrest on a basketball court and now has an ICD.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establish care

54M, HS science teacher, here to establish. Prior PCP retired this spring; records release signed today.

HPI: Feels well. Two longstanding issues:
1. High cholesterol — put on atorvastatin 20 by his old doctor in 2018. Takes it every night, no muscle aches. Doesn't remember his numbers.
2. Low back — achy lower back on and off for years, worse after long days on his feet in the lab or yard work, settles with rest and Tylenol. No radiation down the legs, no numbness or weakness, no bowel or bladder change, no night pain, no weight loss. Uses acetaminophen 500 mg maybe a few times a month.

PMH: hyperlipidemia, chronic mechanical LBP. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: atorvastatin 20 mg nightly; acetaminophen 500 mg PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: Father died suddenly at 64, "his heart," had high blood pressure. Mother — type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol. One sibling with high blood pressure.
SHx: Teaches chemistry and physics at the high school. Smoked about a pack a day for 20 years, quit 2019, no relapses, no vaping. Alcohol a couple of drinks a month. No drugs. Plays pickup basketball on weekends, walks.

ROS: negative except as above. No chest pain, no exertional symptoms on the court, no palpitations, no syncope.

Exam: Well-appearing, NAD. Vitals reviewed and normal, BP fine today. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Back: no midline tenderness, mild paraspinal tightness L>R, full flexion with mild discomfort, SLR negative bilaterally. Strength and reflexes symmetric in the legs. Skin no rash. No edema.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P:
# Hypercholesterolemia — continue atorvastatin 20. Lipids and CMP today.
# Chronic low back pain, mechanical, no red flags — core and hip stretching handout, acetaminophen as needed. Revisit if it limits him.
# Former smoker, 20 pk-yr, quit 4 yrs ago — meets criteria for annual low-dose CT lung screening. Discussed what it can and can't do, false positives. He'd like to do it. Ordered.
# Health maintenance — CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c (mom with diabetes). One-time HIV and hep C screens. Talked through PSA pros/cons; he wants it checked. He says colonoscopy at 50 was clean — will confirm when records arrive. Flu/COVID/Shingrix in October when the fall vaccines are in.

RTC for physical next fall, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Chad — your bloodwork from Tuesday is back. Kidney and liver tests, blood counts and A1c are all normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. PSA is in the normal range for your age. On the atorvastatin your LDL is a little over 100, which is a reasonable place for you right now — keep taking it as you have been. The lung CT scheduling office should be calling you. Have a good start to the school year.

documents.title: Records from Prior Primary Care Practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from prior PCP (practice closed after physician retirement), 38 pages, scanned to media.

Abstracted for the chart:
- Hyperlipidemia; atorvastatin 20 mg started 03/2018. Lipids on file 2019-2022, LDL roughly 100-115 on treatment.
- Screening colonoscopy 2019: no polyps, repeat in 10 years.
- Tdap 06/2014.
- Tobacco: documented ~1 ppd, quit 2019.
- No surgical history listed. BP readings in the old notes all normal.
Forwarded to PCP for review.

reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (BASELINE)
Indication: 54-year-old former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2019.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or pleural effusion. Central airways patent. Heart size normal; no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back to talk about his back. Same pattern he's had for years — dull ache across the low back by the end of a long day, stiff in the mornings for a few minutes. Nothing new. Wants to get ahead of it before he's doing yard work and basketball all summer. Tylenol a few times a month still does the job. O: Vitals ok. Walks normally, heel and toe walk fine. No spinal tenderness. Paraspinal tightness bilat lumbar. Flexion to mid-shin. SLR neg both sides. Strength 5/5 LE, patellar and Achilles reflexes 2+ symmetric. Sensation intact.

A/P: Chronic mechanical low back pain, stable, no red flags, no imaging indicated.

- Pain 3/10 today.
F/u at his physical in the fall.

Outpatient Physical Therapy — Initial Evaluation (seen 04/29/2024)
Referral: chronic mechanical low back pain.

Subjective: Intermittent low back ache for several years, worse with prolonged standing and lifting, eased by rest. Goal: stay active with weekend basketball and yard work without flares.
Objective: Lumbar flexion mildly limited by end-range tightness; extension full. Hip flexor and hamstring tightness bilaterally. Core endurance reduced (plank 35 s). Neuro screen negative; slump and SLR negative.
Assessment: Mechanical low back pain with deconditioning of trunk stabilizers and posterior chain tightness. Good rehab potential.
Plan: 4 visits over 6 weeks, then independent home exercise program. Program issued today; patient demonstrated correctly.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient Physical Therapy — Discharge Summary
Diagnosis: chronic mechanical low back pain.
Visits attended: 4 of 4.
Progress: Reports fewer end-of-day aches and no flares during the treatment period. Trunk endurance and hamstring flexibility improved. Independent and consistent with home exercise program.
Status: Goals met. Discharged to home program. Re-referral welcome if symptoms return.
Thank you for this referral.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

55M. Doing well. Back has behaved since he finished PT in June; does the home exercises "most days." Still on atorvastatin nightly, no side effects. No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations or syncope, including on the basketball court. No headaches or vision change.

Meds: atorvastatin 20 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg prn (rare).
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: teaching, busy fall. Ex-smoker since 2019. ETOH a couple drinks/month.
FHx unchanged: father sudden cardiac death at 64 with HTN; mother DM2/HLD; sibling HTN.

Vitals: BP 148/92 on arrival and about the same sitting quietly at the end of the visit. Others normal. First elevated reading we have for him; old records all normal.

Exam: NAD. Fundi not examined. Neck no bruit. Heart RRR, no murmur, no gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no bruit. Pulses 2+ and equal. No edema. Back nontender.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 1.

A/P:
# Elevated BP without a diagnosis of hypertension yet — one office reading; with his family history this needs follow-through. Buy an upper-arm cuff, check mornings and evenings for a week or two, bring the log. Recheck visit in about a month. Lower salt, keep moving. No medication today.
# Hypercholesterolemia — lipids today, continue atorvastatin 20.
# Lung screening — due, ordered.
# HM: CMP, CBC, A1c today. Flu and COVID given. Shingrix done. Colonoscopy 2019 normal, next 2029. PSA last year normal, will revisit next year.

documents.title: Office Visit — Blood Pressure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP recheck. Brought a neat handwritten log, upper-arm cuff, AM and PM for 12 days: almost all readings in the 150s over the 90s, average about 152/94. No headache, chest pain, visual change, dyspnea or edema. Didn't change much on salt — admits the school cafeteria is a problem.

Office BP today 158/96 (repeat after 5 min similar). HR regular.
Heart RRR no murmur, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P: Essential hypertension — confirmed by home readings and two office visits. Strong family history (father died suddenly at 64 with HTN, sibling HTN). Labs last month: normal creatinine and potassium, A1c normal.
- Start lisinopril 10 mg once daily. Went over side effects: lightheadedness early on, dry cough, rare lip/tongue swelling — stop and call or go to the ED if that happens.
- BMP in about 10 days to check potassium and creatinine; ordered, can go to the lab Friday the 6th.
- Keep logging. Recheck visit Dec 9.
- Diet: salt is the big one for him. DASH handout.

documents.title: Lightheaded
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, since starting the blood pressure pill last week I get a quick lightheaded feeling when I stand up fast. It goes away in a second or two. Otherwise fine. Is that normal or should I stop it? My home numbers are way down. Chad

documents.title: RE: Lightheaded
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Chad, thanks for letting us know. That can happen in the first couple of weeks on lisinopril as your body adjusts to a lower pressure. Keep taking it, stand up in stages, and drink plenty of water. Please still get your bloodwork Friday and keep your visit Monday the 9th so the doctor can check you. If you pass out, feel your heart racing, or the lightheadedness is getting worse, call us right away.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: BMP one week on lisinopril: creatinine and potassium unchanged from October, sodium normal. OK to continue. Will review at Monday's visit.

reports.text: 12-lead ECG at rest. Sinus rhythm. PR, QRS and QT intervals within normal limits. Normal axis. No ST-segment or T-wave abnormality. No prior for comparison.

documents.title: Office Visit — Hypertension Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective: Follow-up of hypertension diagnosed on 11/27. He picked up the lisinopril two days after that visit, so he's 10 days in, hasn't missed a dose. Since starting he's had a brief lightheaded feeling when he stands up fast — getting up from the desk after grading, out of a chair at home. Lasts a second or two, no room-spinning, no blackout, never fallen. Otherwise feels fine. No chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations. No orthopnea or PND, no ankle swelling. No cough so far. Home readings have come down to the 120s/70s-80s.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily (new 11/27), atorvastatin 20 mg, acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.

Objective: BP 120/78, HR 84. Orthostatic check lying then standing at 1 and 3 minutes: no drop meeting orthostatic criteria; he said he felt faintly lightheaded for a moment on first standing, which passed. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Neuro nonfocal, gait normal.
BMP from 12/6: creatinine and electrolytes normal.
ECG today: normal sinus rhythm, normal intervals, no ST-T changes.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Essential hypertension, responding well to lisinopril 10 mg — home and office readings at goal already.
2. Brief lightheadedness on rapid standing, early in ACE-inhibitor therapy, no orthostatic hypotension on testing, normal ECG and labs. Expect it to fade. Rise in stages, keep up fluids, especially on long teaching days. Call if it worsens, if he faints, or if he has palpitations.
- Continue lisinopril 10 mg. Keep checking BP a few times a week.
- Follow-up in 3 months.

events.reason: flame burns of abdominal wall and left flank

conditions.label: Burn of third degree of abdominal wall, initial encounter
conditions.note: deep partial- and full-thickness flame burns, anterior abdominal wall and left flank, about 8% TBSA

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia at 118 beats per minute. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QTc within normal limits. No ST-segment elevation or depression. No arrhythmia.

reports.study: Portable XR Abdomen Supine and Upright
reports.text:
XR ABDOMEN, SUPINE AND UPRIGHT
Indication: distension, vomiting, no flatus, postoperative day 3.
Findings: Gas-distended loops of small bowel and colon throughout the abdomen, with gas extending to the rectum. No discrete transition point. No pneumoperitoneum on the upright view. No pathologic calcification. Skin staples and dressing material project over the lower abdomen and left flank.
reports.conclusion: Diffuse small and large bowel dilatation without transition point, consistent with adynamic (paralytic) ileus. No free air.

documents.title: Patient Call — Hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called from his hospital room to let us know he was admitted Friday night to the burn unit at the regional hospital after a flash fire at home — burns to his belly and left side. Says he is in a lot of discomfort but doing OK, going to the OR tomorrow for skin grafting. Wanted his PCP to know. Asked that they send records. Told him to call when discharged so we can see him within a week. Message to PCP.

documents.title: Burn Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — BURN SURGERY SERVICE (GENERAL SURGERY)
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/25/2025   Discharged: 08/07/2025

Patient: Chad Whitney, 56 M
PCP: notified; copy to PCP
Allergies: NKDA

Admitting diagnosis: Flame burns, anterior abdominal wall and left flank, approximately 8% TBSA, mixed deep partial and full thickness.
Secondary: Sinus tachycardia secondary to burns. Postoperative paralytic ileus (resolved).
Chronic: Hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, chronic low back pain.

History: Flash flame burn at home on the evening of 07/25. Brought in by ambulance. No inhalation injury: no facial burns, no singed nasal hair, voice normal, no carbonaceous sputum. No other trauma.

Hospital course:
- Burns: Initial cleansing and debridement, silver-based dressings. On admission HR 118, sinus tachycardia on ECG, attributed to burn injury and pain; rate ran 100s-110s through the first week and was in the 90s by discharge. Tetanus: last booster 2014, Tdap given on admission. Fluids by mouth with IV maintenance (burn size below formal resuscitation threshold). Home lisinopril and atorvastatin continued.
- 07/29: Tangential excision and split-thickness skin grafting, abdominal wall and left flank; donor site right anterior thigh (see operative note).
- POD 3 (08/01): developed distension, nausea and repeated emesis, no flatus or stool since surgery. Abdominal films: diffuse bowel dilatation without transition point, no free air. K 3.3, Mg 1.6. Diagnosed postoperative paralytic ileus. Managed with NPO, nasogastric decompression, IV fluids, potassium and magnesium repletion, opioid sparing (scheduled acetaminophen), early ambulation. Flatus 08/04, NG removed; BM 08/05; diet advanced without difficulty.
- Graft take good at first and second dressing takedowns. Donor site epithelializing.

Discharge exam: Afebrile, HR 90s, BP normal. Abdomen soft, nondistended, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Grafts adherent, no infection. Donor site clean.

Discharge medications:
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily (unchanged)
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily (unchanged)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg tabs, 1-2 tabs every 6 hours as needed for pain (home medication)
- No opioids prescribed at discharge.
Wound care: dressing supplies and instructions given; teaching done with patient.

Follow-up: Burn clinic 08/14. PCP within 1 week. Return for fever, wound redness or drainage, vomiting, abdominal distension, or no bowel movement for 3 days.

documents.title: Operative Note — Excision and Grafting
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT (date of surgery 07/29/2025)
Preoperative / postoperative diagnosis: Deep partial- and full-thickness flame burns of anterior abdominal wall and left flank, ~8% TBSA.
Procedure: Tangential excision of burn wounds, abdominal wall and left flank. Split-thickness skin autograft to excised beds, meshed, secured with staples. Donor site right anterior thigh.
Anesthesia: General endotracheal.
Findings: Mixed-depth burn with full-thickness areas centrally on the abdominal wall and along the left flank. Excised to viable, bleeding tissue. No fascial involvement.
Blood loss minimal. No transfusion.
Complications: None.
Dressings: Nonadherent layer, bolster, negative-pressure dressing to grafts; donor site with occlusive dressing.
Disposition: To floor, stable.

documents.title: General Surgery Progress Note — POD 3
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
SURGERY PROGRESS NOTE 08/01/2025, hospital day 8, POD 3 s/p excision and grafting of abdominal wall and L flank burns.

S: Abdomen has been getting more bloated each day since the OR. Not hungry. Nauseated, vomited several times overnight and this morning. No flatus and no BM since surgery. Denies fever, chills, chest pain, urinary symptoms. On oxycodone for graft and donor site pain.

O: Afebrile. Abdomen distended but soft. Diffuse mild tenderness, no guarding or rebound, no masses. Bowel sounds markedly diminished. Grafts and donor site clean, no erythema or drainage, NPWT seal intact.
Labs: K 3.3, Mg 1.6, otherwise unremarkable.
KUB supine/upright: diffuse gaseous distension of small and large bowel to rectum, no transition point, no free air.

A/P: Postoperative paralytic ileus — opioids plus immobility, low K and Mg contributing. No sign of obstruction.
- NPO, place NG to low intermittent suction
- IV fluids; replace K and Mg, recheck AM
- Stop oxycodone; scheduled acetaminophen, minimize opioids
- Ambulate in hallway TID
- Serial abdominal exams

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
POST-DISCHARGE VISIT (TCM)
Admitted 7/25-8/7, regional hospital burn service. Discharge summary, op note and surgical notes reviewed.

Course in brief: flash flame burn at home 7/25, mixed deep partial/full thickness to anterior abdominal wall and L flank, ~8% TBSA. Sinus tachycardia on arrival, put down to the burn. Tdap given. Excision and STSG 7/29 (donor R thigh). Postop paralytic ileus POD 3 with K 3.3 / Mg 1.6 — NG, NPO, repletion, opioids stopped; resolved 8/4-8/5.

Today: Home 5 days. Eating normally, BMs daily, no nausea or bloating. Pain manageable with acetaminophen, mostly at dressing changes and the donor site. Sleeping OK. No fever. Doing his own dressing changes per instructions.

Meds reconciled: lisinopril 10 daily, atorvastatin 20 daily, acetaminophen 500 mg 1-2 q6h prn. No opioids. Allergies NKDA.

Exam: HR 98, regular — still a little quick but well down from the 100s-110s he ran in hospital. Afebrile. Down about 3 kg from spring. Abdomen soft, nondistended, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Grafted areas over the abdominal wall and L flank under dressings — the edge I looked at is pink, adherent, no purulence. R anterior thigh donor site dry and healing. Lungs clear.

A/P:
# Burns s/p excision and grafting — healing as expected; burn clinic 8/14.
# Sinus tachycardia from the burn — improving, recheck at burn clinic/next visit.
# Postoperative ileus — resolved. Off the active list.
# HTN — BP fine on lisinopril, continue.
# Electrolytes — BMP and Mg today to make sure K and Mg have stayed up off IV repletion.
Call for fever, increasing redness or drainage, vomiting or belly swelling.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium and magnesium are both back in the normal range, and kidney function is fine. No supplements needed. Good luck at the burn clinic tomorrow.

documents.title: Burn Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
BURN CLINIC — outpatient follow-up (seen 08/14/2025)

56M, 2.5 weeks from tangential excision and STSG to abdominal wall and left flank flame burns.
Doing well at home. Eating, bowels normal. Pain controlled with acetaminophen.

HR 88, afebrile.
Wounds: Grafts adherent throughout, interstices closing, no loss, no infection. Mild expected pinkness. Donor site right thigh nearly epithelialized.

Plan: Switch to daily moisturizing and light dressing as interstices close. Begin gentle scar massage once fully closed. Sun protection to grafted skin. Return in 3 weeks.

reports.text:
EMERGENT CORONARY ANGIOGRAPHY
Indication: Out-of-hospital VF arrest with ROSC; post-ROSC ECG without ST elevation.
Access: Right radial artery. Patient intubated and sedated.
Left main: Normal.
Left anterior descending: No obstructive disease.
Left circumflex: No obstructive disease.
Right coronary artery: Dominant, no obstructive disease.
No dissection, thrombus or anomalous origin.
Hemostasis with radial band. No complications.
reports.conclusion: No obstructive coronary artery disease. No culprit lesion. No intervention.

reports.text:
TRANSTHORACIC ECHOCARDIOGRAM
Indication: post-cardiac arrest.
Left ventricle: Normal size and wall thickness. LVEF 55% by biplane method. No regional wall-motion abnormality.
Right ventricle: Normal size and systolic function.
Atria: Normal size.
Valves: Structurally normal; no significant stenosis or regurgitation.
Pericardium: No effusion.
Aorta: Normal root dimension.
reports.conclusion: Normal LV size and function, LVEF 55%. Normal RV. No significant valve disease.

reports.text:
CARDIAC MRI WITH AND WITHOUT GADOLINIUM
Indication: Ventricular fibrillation arrest, coronary angiography without obstructive disease; evaluate for cardiomyopathy or scar.
LV: Normal size, normal wall thickness, normal global and regional systolic function. LVEF 58%.
RV: Normal size and function.
T2-weighted imaging: No myocardial edema.
Late gadolinium enhancement: None.
Valves and pericardium: Normal.
reports.conclusion: Normal biventricular size and function, LVEF 58%. No late gadolinium enhancement or edema. No structural substrate for ventricular arrhythmia identified.

documents.title: Call from Hospital Case Manager
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Case manager from the regional hospital CICU called: our patient was admitted Saturday 3/14 after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest at a gym, VF, bystander CPR, ROSC in the ED. Cath showed no blockages. He was cooled and was extubated this morning, waking up appropriately per her. EP is involved and an ICD is likely before discharge. They asked for a current med list and allergies — faxed. Requested records at discharge. PCP notified; will need a post-discharge visit within a week of going home.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 03/14/2026, arrival 10:44
Patient: Chad Whitney, 57 M
Allergies: NKDA

Chief complaint: Cardiac arrest.

HPI (from EMS and bystanders): Collapsed suddenly around 10:20 while playing a pickup basketball game at a local gym. Found unresponsive and not breathing. One bystander with basic life support training began chest compressions immediately while another called 911. EMS arrived to good-quality bystander CPR in progress. Initial rhythm VF. EMS delivered 3 defibrillations with epinephrine and amiodarone 300 mg IV; VF persisted. Transported with ongoing compressions.
PMH per records: hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, chronic low back pain. Prior evaluation for orthostatic lightheadedness after starting antihypertensive (12/2024). Postoperative ileus after burn excision and grafting (2025).
Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg PRN.
FHx: father with sudden cardiac death at 64, HTN; mother DM2, HLD; sibling HTN.
Social: high school science teacher; ex-smoker, 20 pack-years, quit about 7 years ago; alcohol 2-3 drinks/month.

Exam on arrival: Pulseless and apneic, compressions in progress. Monitor: ventricular fibrillation.

ED course:
10:46 Defibrillation #4. Compressions resumed. Epinephrine.
10:49 Amiodarone 150 mg IV. Defibrillation #5 — VF persists.
10:50 Intubated, ETT position confirmed with waveform capnography. Labs sent.
10:51 Lidocaine 100 mg IV. Pads changed to anterior-posterior.
10:52 Defibrillation #6 (vector change). Organized rhythm, palpable pulse — ROSC about 32 minutes after collapse. Epinephrine 4 mg total, prehospital and ED.
11:00 Post-ROSC 12-lead: sinus tachycardia 108, no ST elevation, QTc 448 ms.
Labs: K 3.9, Mg 2.0, lactate 7.8, hs-troponin I 64 ng/L.
Cardiology at bedside; to cath lab emergently.

Impression: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest from refractory ventricular fibrillation, ROSC after 6 defibrillations.
Disposition: Cardiac catheterization lab, then CICU.

documents.title: Electrophysiology Consultation
documents.author: electrophysiology
documents.body:
CARDIAC ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY CONSULTATION (03/19/2026)
Reason: VF arrest, ICD evaluation.

57M with HTN and hyperlipidemia, ex-smoker, who had a witnessed out-of-hospital arrest during basketball on 3/14. VF refractory to 5 shocks, ROSC after the 6th with a vector change. Angiography: no obstructive CAD. Echo LVEF 55%, cardiac MRI LVEF 58% with no LGE or edema. K and Mg normal on arrival. Post-ROSC ECG without ST elevation, QTc 448 ms; serial ECGs without Brugada pattern or pre-excitation. No ventricular ectopy of note on telemetry since ROSC. Off sedation, neurologically intact; no memory of the day.

Family history: father died suddenly at 64.

Impression: VF cardiac arrest without an identified reversible cause or structural heart disease.

Recommendations:
1. Secondary-prevention ICD — transvenous single-chamber system, left pectoral; discussed risks, benefits and alternatives, he agrees. Planned 3/20.
2. Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily.
3. Continue lisinopril and atorvastatin.
4. Given his father's sudden death, offered referral for cardiac genetic counseling and testing. He would like time to think it over and talk to his sibling; no testing sent.
5. No driving for 6 months from the arrest.
6. Device clinic in 1 week, EP clinic in 4 weeks, remote monitoring enrollment.

documents.title: ICD Implantation
documents.author: electrophysiology
documents.body:
PROCEDURE NOTE — date of procedure 03/20/2026
Procedure: Implantation of transvenous single-chamber implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, left pectoral.
Indication: Secondary prevention after VF cardiac arrest without reversible cause.
Anesthesia: Moderate sedation and local anesthesia.
Description: Left axillary vein access under fluoroscopic guidance. Single-coil defibrillator lead positioned at the RV apical septum; sensing, impedance and threshold values satisfactory and stable. Lead secured, connected to generator placed in a left prepectoral pocket. Pocket irrigated, layered closure, skin adhesive.
Defibrillation testing: not performed.
Programming: VF zone with shock therapy; VT monitor zone. 
Complications: None. Post-procedure chest film: lead in good position, no pneumothorax.
Plan: Arm sling overnight; no lifting the left arm above the shoulder for 4 weeks. Device clinic wound check in 7-10 days.

documents.title: Cardiology Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIOLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/14/2026   Discharged 03/23/2026
Principal diagnosis: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to refractory ventricular fibrillation.
Procedures: Emergent coronary angiography (3/14). Transvenous single-chamber ICD (3/20).
Other: Hypertension. Hypercholesterolemia. Chronic low back pain.
Allergies: NKDA

Course:
Arrested during basketball 3/14; bystander CPR, 6 defibrillations in all, ROSC ~32 minutes after collapse (see ED record). Emergent angiography: no obstructive coronary disease. To CICU on the ventilator; temperature control at 36 C for 24 hours, then controlled normothermia. hs-troponin I 64 on arrival, peak 2,310 ng/L at 12 hours, consistent with CPR and multiple shocks in the absence of coronary disease. TTE 3/15: LVEF 55%, no regional abnormality. Extubated 3/16; by 3/17 awake, oriented, following commands, no focal neurological deficit; amnestic for the event. Cardiac MRI 3/18: normal size and function, LVEF 58%, no LGE or edema. No recurrent ventricular arrhythmia on telemetry after ROSC. Electrolytes normal throughout. EP: VF without identified reversible cause; secondary-prevention ICD placed 3/20 without complication. Metoprolol succinate started. Genetic evaluation offered; patient undecided.

Condition at discharge: Good. Ambulating independently. Chest wall sore from CPR.

Discharge medications:
- Metoprolol succinate ER 25 mg daily — NEW
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily
- Acetaminophen 500 mg 1-2 tabs every 6 hours as needed

Instructions: No driving for 6 months (through 9/14/2026). No lifting left arm above shoulder for 4 weeks. Keep incision dry until the device clinic check. Carry device ID card. If you receive a shock and feel well, call the device clinic; if more than one shock or you feel unwell, call 911.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week. Device clinic 3/31. EP clinic in 4 weeks. Remote monitor set up before discharge.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit — Cardiac Arrest
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM VISIT. Hospital 3/14-3/23. ED record, cath, echo, MRI, EP consult, ICD note and discharge summary all reviewed.

Summary: Witnessed collapse playing basketball 3/14, bystander CPR right away, VF refractory to multiple shocks — ROSC after the 6th (~32 min). Cath: no obstructive CAD. Cooled 24 h. Echo EF 55%, MRI EF 58% with no scar. K/Mg normal. Neurologically intact. EP calls it VF without a reversible cause; transvenous single-chamber ICD 3/20 for secondary prevention, metoprolol succinate 25 added. Genetics offered given father's sudden death at 64 — he hasn't decided.

Today: Came with a friend who drove. Tired, naps in the afternoon. Front of the chest is sore where they did compressions, a little better every day, worse rolling over in bed. No chest pressure with walking, no palpitations, no lightheadedness, no fainting, no shocks. Remembers nothing from the morning of the game until waking in the ICU. Sleep a bit broken. Mood "grateful, a little rattled." Walking 10-15 minutes around the block.

Meds reconciled: metoprolol succinate ER 25 mg daily (new), lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, acetaminophen prn. Allergies NKDA.

Exam: BP 118/74, HR 62 regular. Alert, conversant, recall of our past visits intact. Left prepectoral ICD pocket: incision closed with skin glue, no hematoma, no erythema. Sternal and parasternal tenderness to palpation, no crepitus. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. R wrist radial site healed. Abdomen: healed grafts. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.
PHQ-9 4, GAD-7 3.

A/P:
# Out-of-hospital VF arrest, refractory, survived neurologically intact; ICD in place, on metoprolol. Device clinic 3/31, EP late April. Reviewed shock plan from discharge papers. Reviewed driving: none until 9/14 per EP.
# Chest wall soreness after CPR — expected; acetaminophen as needed. Should keep easing.
# HTN — BP and HR fine on lisinopril plus metoprolol. BMP today.
# Hypercholesterolemia — atorvastatin 20.
# Fatigue and adjustment after the arrest — normal screens today; talked about how common it is to feel shaken for a while. He knows to reach out.
# Work — out of work for now; note given. Return date once EP has seen him.
F/u 3 months or sooner.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:
Mr. Chad Whitney has been under hospital and outpatient care since March 14, 2026, and is unable to work at this time. I anticipate an update on his return date after his cardiology appointment in late April.

documents.title: Device Clinic — Wound Check
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DEVICE CLINIC (03/31/2026)
Single-chamber transvenous ICD, implanted 03/20/2026, secondary prevention after VF arrest.
Incision: well healed, no hematoma, no erythema or drainage.
Interrogation: Battery and lead parameters normal and stable since implant. Underlying rhythm sinus. No arrhythmia episodes recorded; no therapies delivered.
Remote monitor transmitting.
Plan: Lift restriction left arm continues through 4 weeks post-implant. EP clinic as scheduled.
cc: PCP

documents.title: Electrophysiology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: electrophysiology
documents.body:
EP CLINIC (04/21/2026)

Mr. Whitney returns one month after VF arrest and secondary-prevention ICD. He feels close to normal. Chest wall soreness from CPR has mostly gone. Walking 30-40 minutes daily without symptoms. No palpitations, presyncope or shocks. Tolerating metoprolol.

Device: normal function; no arrhythmia episodes; no therapies.
Exam: Regular, pocket healed.

Assessment: Idiopathic VF arrest with ICD, stable.
Plan:
- May return to teaching 04/27/2026.
- Driving restriction stands until 09/14/2026.
- Continue walking and gradually build moderate exercise; hold off on competitive basketball for now, we will revisit.
- Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily.
- Genetics: still undecided; referral remains available whenever he wants it.
- Remote monitoring; EP visit with interrogation in 3 months.
cc: PCP

Battery: normal. Lead impedance, sensing and threshold trends: stable, within normal limits.
Episodes: none. Therapies: none.
Presenting rhythm: sinus.
Impression: Normal device function. No arrhythmia. Next remote transmission in 3 months; EP clinic in July.
cc: PCP

documents.title: Electrophysiology Clinic — Device Follow-up
documents.author: electrophysiology
documents.body:
EP CLINIC WITH DEVICE INTERROGATION (07/14/2026)
Four months after VF arrest, single-chamber ICD for secondary prevention.
Asymptomatic. Exercising regularly at moderate intensity. No shocks.
Interrogation: Battery and lead function normal. No ventricular arrhythmia episodes; no therapies since implant. Remote transmissions have been normal.
Medications: metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Plan: Continue metoprolol. Remote monitoring every 3 months; clinic in 6 months. Driving may resume after 09/14/2026 if no events. Return to basketball to be discussed at the next visit. Genetic referral still open if he wishes.
cc: PCP
